raw_case_text: At 12 years of age the patient was admitted with gastroenteritis, generalized intestinal edema and severe nephrotic syndrome progressing to acute renal failure. Quantitative CMV PCR was positive >2 x 106 copies/ml in blood and positive in a renal biopsy (not quantified in tissue). Renal histology showed focal-segmental glomerulosclerosis with extracapillary hypercellularity and mild tubulointerstitial atrophy. Ultrastructural findings showed complete pedicellar effacement characteristic of minimal change nephropathy and no intracellular inclusions or antibody deposits were demonstrated on cytopathology (Figure 1D). Immunofluorescence was faintly positive for C3 and IgG and negative for C1q, IgA, IgM, and fibrin. Exome files were screened for pathogenic podocin mutations that can be associated with nephrotic syndrome, and no pathogenic variants were identified. Interestingly, elevations in CMV titers in blood seemed to precede nephrotic syndrome relapses and correlate with increases in proteinuria (Figure 1F). Due to chronic systemic CMV infection and severe nephrotic syndrome with acute renal failure, she required intermittent critical level care and treatment with systemic steroids. She also received IVIG, broad-spectrum antibiotics, Pneumocystis jiroveci prophylaxis with cotrimoxazole, ganciclovir progressing to foscarnet due to proven resistant CMV strains and hyperimmune CMV-specific immunoglobulin (Cytogam ). Despite aggressive anti-viral therapy, it was impossible to fully control the CMV infection or the nephrotic syndrome that fluctuated in accordance with blood CMV titers that remained between 1 x 106 and 4 x 106 copies/ml despite aggressive treatment. Immunosuppressive therapy, first mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) later cyclosporine were initiated. She had an initial response to this treatment achieving reduction of proteinuria. Unfortunately, CMV infection could not be cleared and the nephrotic syndrome finally became unresponsive to treatment. In this clinical context stem cell transplant was not feasible. During this final end stage disease, she developed Pneumocytis jiroveci pneumonia and fungal lung infection (Figure 1E). Bronchoalveolar lavage was positive for Pneumocystis jiroveci, CMV and galactomannan. She progressed to multi-organ failure and died at 13 years of age, 1 year after her initial admission for nephrotic syndrome associated with systemic CMV infection.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 12-year-old girl with severe systemic cytomegalovirus-associated focal segmental glomerulosclerosis and nephrotic syndrome developed end-stage opportunistic Pneumocystis jirovecii and fungal pneumonia at 13 years of age following prolonged immunosuppressive therapy.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Admitted at 12 years of age with gastroenteritis, generalized intestinal edema, and severe nephrotic syndrome progressing to acute renal failure, the patient was found to have high-level systemic cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection (>2 x 10^6 copies/mL in blood and positive in renal biopsy tissue) driving biopsy-proven focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) with podocyte foot-process effacement. Over the ensuing year, her persistent CMV viremia (1 x 10^6 to 4 x 10^6 copies/mL) proved refractory to ganciclovir, foscarnet (for resistant CMV strains), CMV-specific hyperimmune globulin (CytoGam), and IVIG, while her relapsing nephrotic syndrome was treated with systemic corticosteroids, mycophenolate mofetil (MMF), and cyclosporine alongside co-trimoxazole prophylaxis. At 13 years of age, during refractory end-stage disease, she developed severe opportunistic pulmonary infection.
subjective.past_medical_history: Severe nephrotic syndrome / focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS; podocin exome screening negative) associated with chronic refractory drug-resistant systemic cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection since age 12.
subjective.review_of_systems: Initial presentation positive for gastroenteritis, generalized edema, and oliguria/renal failure; terminal stage at age 13 positive for severe respiratory failure.

objective.physical_examination: Generalized edema and nephrotic syndrome at baseline, progressing to critical illness and multiorgan failure at age 13.
objective.routine_investigations: Virological monitoring: Persistent high-grade plasma CMV DNAemia (initially >2 x 10^6 copies/mL, fluctuating between 1 x 10^6 and 4 x 10^6 copies/mL in parallel with proteinuria relapses).
objective.advanced_workup: Renal biopsy (age 12) and exome screening: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) with extracapillary hypercellularity, mild tubulointerstitial atrophy, faint C3/IgG immunofluorescence, complete podocyte foot-process effacement on electron microscopy without viral inclusions, and positive tissue CMV PCR; whole-exome screening negative for pathogenic podocin mutations. Terminal-stage chest imaging and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL, age 13): Severe pulmonary infiltrates; BAL fluid tested positive for Pneumocystis jirovecii, cytomegalovirus (CMV), and Aspergillus galactomannan.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Fatal polymicrobial opportunistic pneumonia with Pneumocystis jirovecii, cytomegalovirus (CMV), and invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (confirmed by positive BAL for P. jirovecii, CMV, and galactomannan) complicating refractory antiviral-resistant systemic CMV infection and steroid/MMF/cyclosporine-treated nephrotic syndrome (FSGS). Plan and clinical course: Despite intensive care, systemic corticosteroids, MMF, cyclosporine, IVIG, CytoGam, ganciclovir, foscarnet, and prior co-trimoxazole prophylaxis, she was ineligible for stem cell transplantation due to uncontrolled CMV and renal failure, progressed to multiorgan failure, and died at 13 years of age.
